Cinderclaw was once an Omega Flameruff of an Emberpup family.
In his youth, he was the flashiest Emberpup around. Every day, he chased the old Omega’s tail and challenged him, getting a mouthful of mud every time he fell, only to climb back up again. Then one day, he finally won. The old Omega gave him one last look, then turned and walked down from the peak.
"I won," Cinderclaw told himself. "I am the strongest now."
But he soon learned that becoming the strongest was not the end. It meant more challenges.
Young Emberpups challenged him one after another, each trying to prove they were stronger than the Omega. Cinderclaw defeated them again and again, but every victory left him a little more tired.
"Am I getting old?" Cinderclaw began to ask himself.
His flame still burned bright. His strength was still mighty. But his heart had begun to age. He started to fear defeat, not because of defeat itself, but because defeat would mean, "I am old. I cannot do this anymore."
That feeling reached its peak on the day he was defeated by a young Emberpup.
That day, Cinderclaw lay on the ground and looked up at the young Flameruff standing before him, eyes full of hunger for victory. Cinderclaw remembered himself from long ago, the Emberpup who would not stop chasing the old Omega’s tail.
"I lost," Cinderclaw said. "The Omega’s place is yours now."
He felt a wave of relief, followed by a crushing sense of loss. He did not know what else he could do. He had been the Omega for too long, grown too used to the pack looking up to him, and forgotten how to be an ordinary wolf.
"Maybe I should go to Thousand-Fang Ridge," Cinderclaw told himself. "Now that I have set down the burden of being Omega, maybe... I should go wild one last time."
He challenged Icho.
Then, everything ended.
With a single strike, Icho knocked Cinderclaw down. Cinderclaw lay on the ground of Thousand-Fang Ridge, gazed at the withered Ridgeback Trees, and suddenly laughed.
"I really am too old," he said. "So old I do not even have the strength to stand."
But after he fell, something he never expected happened. A legend began to spread across Beast Fang Ridge: the "Immortal Warrior."
They say that after the defeated old Omega left the peak, he still left his footprints all across Beast Fang Ridge. He taught young Emberpups how to fight, helped injured Emberpups find their way home, and even drove off an entire Bonesky family alone during one raid.
"He did not grow old. He just found another way to fight," said the Emberpups he had helped.
But Cinderclaw did not know any of this. He was trapped in Thousand-Fang Ridge and became an Inferlupa. Around his feet was a chain called "old age," and over his heart lay a layer of dust called "powerlessness."
"I am too old," Cinderclaw told himself. "Too old to do anything."
But he did not know that beneath the peak, flames can still burn. Leaving the summit may not be the end. It may be the beginning of passing on the torch.
